'''Aretha Leonore Teckentrup''' is a UK-based mathematician, known for her research on [[uncertainty quantification]] and [[numerical analysis]]. Her work focuses on [[multilevel Monte Carlo method]]s for the [[Numerical methods for partial differential equations|numerical solution of partial differential equations]], [[Gaussian processes]] and [[Bayesian inference]].{{r|whitehead}} She is a reader in the mathematics of data science at the [[University of Edinburgh]].{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
Teckentrup was a student in mathematics at the [[University of Bath]] beginning in 2005. She earned a master's degree there in 2009, and completed her PhD in 2013.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Multilevel Monte Carlo methods and Uncertainty Quantification'', was supervised by Robert Scheichl.{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research with [[Max Gunzburger]] at [[Florida State University]] from 2013 to 2014 and with [[Andrew M. Stuart]] at the [[University of Warwick]] from 2014 to 2016, she became a lecturer at the University of Edinburgh in 2016.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Teckentrup was a second-place winner of the [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]] in 2017.{{r|fox}} In 2018 she became the inaugural winner of the SIAG/Uncertainty Quantification Early Career Prize of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] Activity Group on Uncertainty Quantification.{{r|siag}} She was one of the 2021 winners of the [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]].{{r|whitehead}}
